title: A Cipher for the Drop
premise: Theo Vane, a data analyst blacklisted by three intelligence agencies for asking the wrong questions, notices that Flight 4471 has been erased from every database while still airborne — including its ninety-one passengers. The vanished flight was carrying a sealed inheritance: evidence of a decades-old extrajudicial assassination program, left to Theo by a father they never knew. Hunted by both the program's surviving architects and a rogue justice collective who want the evidence released without trial, Theo must decide whether truth served through official channels is worth more than justice delivered outside them. In the end, Theo trades the archive's location to the collective in exchange for the passengers' names being made public — burning their own credibility forever, but forcing one honest reckoning into the light.
about_author: B. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former records auditor who spent eleven years inside government archives before walking away with nothing but questions. They write thrillers about paper trails, dead files, and the people who refuse to stop reading.

chapters.title: Ninety-One Ghosts
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Working freelance data forensics from a rented room, Theo cross-references aviation manifests for a routine client and finds Flight 4471 missing mid-flight — no crash report, no landing record, nothing. The emotional beat is cold dread sharpening into obsession as Theo realizes the erasure is too clean to be an error.

chapters.title: The Letter That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Digging into the passenger list, Theo discovers their own estranged father, Emil Vane, was aboard — and that probate records name Theo sole heir to an unopened deposit box. The beat is vertigo: grief for a man they resented colliding with the suspicion that his death was engineered.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, One Door
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo visits a former handler, Marisol Quist, hoping old loyalties buy answers; she warns them off and slips them a burner phone anyway. The emotional beat is bitter tenderness — proof someone still cares, wrapped in confirmation that Theo is already being watched.

chapters.title: Deposit Box 4471
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In a Basel bank vault, Theo opens the box to find a ledger of codenames, dates, and one word repeated across pages: DROP. A silent alarm trips as they leave. The beat is exhilaration curdling into panic — the inheritance is real, and it is radioactive.

chapters.title: The Man Who Offers Rides
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Callum Reyes, a courteous fixer for the program's architects, who offers Theo protection in exchange for the ledger. His charm makes the threat worse. The beat is seductive menace: the first time Theo understands this is a negotiation where refusal is fatal.

chapters.title: Rules I Used to Believe
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Flashback chapter to Theo's dismissal from the third agency — reporting a falsified drone assessment and being made the scapegoat instead. The beat is wounded idealism, showing why Theo can't simply hand the ledger to authorities and trust the machine.

chapters.title: The Collective Leaves a Card
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A stranger named Wren intercepts Theo in a train station, revealing a network of ex-operatives who execute justice the law abandoned — and who want the ledger's evidence released on their terms. The beat is temptation: for the first time, someone offers Theo a way to matter.

chapters.title: Quist Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reports her contact with Theo up the chain and realizes her own superiors are scrubbing her access — she is being cut loose as collateral. The beat is dawning betrayal as the loyalist discovers loyalty runs one direction.

chapters.title: Copy, Then Burn
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo photographs the ledger and hides fragments in three cities, then destroys the original to force all parties to negotiate rather than kill. The beat is grim empowerment: the burnt analyst finally holds leverage, and hates how good it feels.

chapters.title: Reyes Makes It Personal
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Ordered to escalate, Callum stages a break-in at Theo's sister Nadia's home — a warning shot, no harm done, message received. The beat is professional guilt cracking through Callum's polish, seeding his eventual turn.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Names
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Decoding the ledger with Wren's cryptographers, Theo learns the DROP was a 1998 operation that killed civilians and was buried by all three of Theo's former agencies — and that Emil Vane was the analyst who tried to expose it. The beat is inherited purpose: Theo's father's fight becomes theirs.

chapters.title: The Auction Nobody Admits
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The collective debates internally: some want public release, others want blackmail leverage over the agencies. Wren must secure Theo's trust while concealing the schism. The beat is uneasy alliance — allies with knives half-drawn.

chapters.title: Marisol's Last Favor
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Officially severed, Marisol uses her final credentials to pull the flight's true manifest and sends it to Theo before going dark. The beat is costly loyalty: she chooses Theo over the institution and pays for it immediately.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Courtesy
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum detains Theo for a 'conversation' that is really an offer: immunity, reinstatement, a clean life — if the ledger dies. For the first time he lies to his employers about what Theo said. The beat is a crack widening into a fault line.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo comes out of hiding to warn Nadia, and the sisters argue about their father — his absence, his secrets, his death. The beat is raw family reckoning: Theo realizes they're repeating Emil's mistake of carrying the burden alone.

chapters.title: The Drop Site
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following Emil's coded annotations, Theo locates the physical DROP archive — a decommissioned relay station holding hard copies the digital erasure missed. The beat is triumph shadowed by horror at the scale of what was buried.

chapters.title: Everyone Comes for the Same Room
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. Reyes's team, a splinter faction of the collective, and agency contractors converge on the relay station simultaneously. A firefight breaks out; Wren is wounded shielding Theo. The beat is chaos as every hidden agenda turns violent at once.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cornered in the archive room with Callum — now openly turned against his employers — Theo negotiates: the hard copies go to the collective's public-release faction, and in exchange the full passenger list of Flight 4471 goes to the press within seventy-two hours. The beat is high-wire resolve: Theo bets everything on strangers keeping their word.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, recovered and off-grid. She helps verify the release while agency lawyers scramble to suppress it; Reyes's former masters order scorched earth. The beat is breathless countdown, each hour bought with a small betrayal of the old order.

chapters.title: Publication
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The names run: ninety-one passengers, the DROP operation, the cover chain reaching two sitting officials. Hearings are announced. Two collective members who wanted leverage are exposed by their own side. The beat is catharsis with teeth — victory that costs Theo every credential they ever had.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Was For
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Testifying under a grant of limited immunity, Callum burns the program's architects, choosing truth over the only loyalty he ever knew. He and Theo meet once afterward, no apologies needed. The beat is quiet absolution between two people who broke the rules for the right reason.

chapters.title: A Cipher, Solved
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Months later, Theo visits Emil's grave with the decoded ledger's final page — a note to his child: 'Some truths are inheritances. Spend them well.' Theo takes new work auditing cold cases, outside every agency. The beat is earned peace: justice outside the law, carried forward on purpose.
